rules.statement: Persist an owner's settings as a separate wrapped object with its own concurrency token, and edit them only through a dedicated settings sub-resource; leave settings off the core resource response and update request, and set initial values only on create.
rules.why: Every settings owner then has the same shape and keeps its own optimistic concurrency, separate from edits to the core resource.
rules.check: Look for a new or changed owner entity that stores settings as a bare JsonElement with no concurrency token of its own, or a resource/update contract that still has a Settings property instead of a .../settings endpoint.

rules.statement: Model every entity that can hold key material (signing secrets, decryption keys) as a secret owner: give it a nested secret collection with its own concurrency token, the standard store CRUD methods, and the standard secrets endpoints that reveal secret material only once.
rules.why: Key material belongs to its owner's boundary, so all secret owners should be addressed the same way and follow the same reveal-once policy.
rules.check: Look for key material added to an entity outside a secrets collection, or a secret owner missing the standard secret store methods or endpoints, or one that returns secret material after creation.

rules.statement: When an owner entity is deleted, cascade the delete to its dependent child collections, including its secrets.
rules.why: Owners clean up after themselves, so no orphaned secret material is left behind.
rules.check: Look for a new child table or collection under an owner, such as secrets, that is not set to cascade-delete in the EF model or migration.
